subject: computer-science
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What does the term 'digital divide' describe?
options: The gap between people who have access to digital technology and those who do not
The boundary between a computer's hardware and its software
A technique for splitting binary numbers during arithmetic
The point at which a network is divided into subnets
questions.explain: The digital divide is the inequality between those who can access and use digital technology and those who cannot.

questions.q: An 'ethical' issue in computing is best described as a concern about what is:
options: Morally right or wrong
Illegal under an Act of Parliament
Harmful to wildlife and habitats
Too expensive for a company to afford
questions.explain: Ethical issues concern moral principles of right and wrong, separate from what is legal or environmental.

questions.q: Which piece of UK legislation makes it an offence to gain unauthorised access to computer material?
options: The Computer Misuse Act 1990
The Copyright, Designs and Patents Act 1988
The Data Protection Act 2018
The Freedom of Information Act 2000
questions.explain: The Computer Misuse Act 1990 criminalises unauthorised access to and modification of computer material, such as hacking.

questions.q: Which UK law primarily governs how organisations must handle and protect people's personal data?
options: The Data Protection Act 2018
The Computer Misuse Act 1990
The Copyright, Designs and Patents Act 1988
The Health and Safety at Work Act 1974
questions.explain: The Data Protection Act 2018 regulates how organisations collect, store and process personal data.

questions.q: Which legislation protects the intellectual property of original works such as software, music and text?
options: The Copyright, Designs and Patents Act 1988
The Computer Misuse Act 1990
The Data Protection Act 2018
The Consumer Rights Act 2015
questions.explain: The Copyright, Designs and Patents Act 1988 protects original creative and technical works, including software.

questions.q: What is meant by 'e-waste'?
options: Discarded electronic and electrical devices
Emails sent in bulk as spam
Energy wasted by leaving devices on standby
Errors produced when data is transmitted
questions.explain: E-waste is discarded electronic equipment such as old phones, computers and televisions.

questions.q: Why is the disposal of e-waste in landfill an environmental concern?
options: It can contain toxic materials that leak into soil and water
It increases the number of radio signals in the atmosphere
It makes broadband connections run more slowly
It uses up the world's supply of binary code
questions.explain: Electronic devices contain toxic substances such as lead and mercury that can pollute the environment if sent to landfill.

questions.q: What is a key feature of open source software?
options: Its source code is freely available for users to view and modify
It can only be run on Apple computers
It always costs more than proprietary software
It cannot be shared with other people
questions.explain: Open source software makes its source code available so it can be studied, modified and redistributed.

questions.q: Why do web cookies raise privacy concerns for users?
options: They can track a user's browsing activity and build a profile of them
They physically damage the hard drive over time
They stop websites from loading images
They convert personal data into binary automatically
questions.explain: Cookies can record browsing behaviour, allowing companies to track users and build detailed profiles of them.

questions.q: Which of these is a common ethical concern about increased automation and use of robots in industry?
options: It can lead to unemployment as machines replace human workers
It makes electricity impossible to generate
It prevents companies from making any profit
It stops data from being stored on computers
questions.explain: Automation can improve efficiency but raises ethical concerns about job losses when machines replace human roles.

questions.q: Why do large data centres have a significant environmental impact?
options: They consume large amounts of electricity to power and cool the servers
They emit large quantities of radioactive waste
They require huge volumes of paper to operate
They release binary data into the atmosphere
questions.explain: Data centres use vast amounts of energy running and cooling servers, much of which may come from non-renewable sources.

questions.q: How can the digital divide disadvantage people who lack reliable internet access?
options: They may struggle to access online education, jobs and government services
They are unable to breathe clean air
They automatically break the Computer Misuse Act
They cannot legally own any electronic device
questions.explain: People without good digital access can be excluded from opportunities such as online learning, employment and public services.

questions.q: Which action would most likely breach the Computer Misuse Act 1990?
options: Logging into someone else's account without permission to read their files
Backing up your own documents to the cloud
Writing an original program and selling it
Deleting files from your own computer
questions.explain: Gaining unauthorised access to someone else's account or data is an offence under the Computer Misuse Act 1990.

questions.q: How does recycling old electronic devices benefit the environment?
options: It recovers valuable materials and reduces toxic waste going to landfill
It increases the amount of e-waste sent to landfill
It removes the need for any electricity generation
It prevents software from ever needing updates
questions.explain: Recycling reclaims useful metals and keeps harmful materials out of landfill, reducing environmental damage.

questions.q: Why is it important that organisations only keep personal data for as long as it is needed?
options: Holding excessive or outdated personal data increases privacy risks if it is misused or leaked
Deleting data is illegal under all circumstances
Storing data forever makes computers run faster
Personal data cannot be stored digitally at all
questions.explain: Keeping unnecessary personal data increases the risk and impact of breaches, so data should be retained only while needed.

questions.q: Which statement best explains why some organisations choose proprietary software over open source software?
options: Proprietary software usually comes with official support and guaranteed updates from the vendor
Proprietary software always allows anyone to edit its source code
Proprietary software is never protected by copyright
Proprietary software cannot contain any errors
questions.explain: Proprietary software is typically backed by professional support and regular vendor updates, which organisations may value.

questions.q: A student guesses a teacher's password and logs in to view exam papers stored on the school system. Which law has the student most clearly broken?
options: The Computer Misuse Act 1990
The Copyright, Designs and Patents Act 1988
The Health and Safety at Work Act 1974
The Freedom of Information Act 2000
questions.explain: Accessing a system without authorisation by using someone else's password is an offence under the Computer Misuse Act 1990.

questions.q: A company wants to reduce the environmental impact of its IT. Which action would most directly help?
options: Powering its data centre with renewable energy and recycling old hardware
Buying new laptops for every employee each month
Sending all old devices straight to landfill
Leaving all servers running at full power overnight
questions.explain: Using renewable energy and recycling hardware lowers both energy-related emissions and e-waste.

questions.q: A shopping website shares customers' email addresses with advertisers without asking permission. Which type of law is this most relevant to?
options: Data protection legislation covering personal data
Copyright legislation covering original works
Computer misuse legislation covering hacking
Environmental legislation covering waste disposal
questions.explain: Sharing customers' personal data without consent is a data protection issue, as personal data must be handled lawfully.

questions.q: A developer makes their app free, releases the source code publicly and lets others modify it. This is an example of:
options: Open source software
Proprietary software
Unauthorised access
Copyright infringement
questions.explain: Releasing free software with publicly available, modifiable source code is the defining feature of open source software.

specSource: AQA GCSE Computer Science (8525) specification; Ethical Legal & Environmental Impacts
